**Makalu**[[4]](#cite_note-Searle2013-5) ([Nepali](/wiki/Nepali_language "Nepali language"): मकालु हिमाल, romanized: *Makālu himāl*; [Chinese](/wiki/Chinese_language "Chinese language"): 马卡鲁峰; [pinyin](/wiki/Pinyin "Pinyin"): *Mǎkǎlǔ Fēng*) is the [fifth-highest mountain](/wiki/List_of_highest_mountains#List "List of highest mountains") on Earth, with a [summit](/wiki/Summit "Summit") at an [elevation](/wiki/Elevation "Elevation") of 8,485 metres (27,838 ft) [AMSL](/wiki/Height_above_mean_sea_level "Height above mean sea level"). It is located in the [Mahalangur](/wiki/Mahalangur_Himal "Mahalangur Himal") [Himalayas](/wiki/Himalayas "Himalayas") 19 km (12 mi) southeast of [Mount Everest](/wiki/Mount_Everest "Mount Everest"), on the [China](/wiki/China "China")–[Nepal](/wiki/Nepal "Nepal") border. One of the [eight-thousanders](/wiki/Eight-thousander "Eight-thousander"), Makalu is an isolated peak shaped like a four-sided [pyramid](/wiki/Pyramidal_peak "Pyramidal peak").

Makalu has two notable subsidiary peaks. Kangchungtse, or Makalu II (7,678 m (25,190 ft)), lies about three kilometres (two miles) north-northwest of the main summit. Rising about 5 km (3 mi) north-northeast of the main summit across a broad plateau, and connected to Kangchungtse by a narrow, 7,200 m (23,600 ft) [saddle](/wiki/Glossary_of_climbing_terms#saddle "Glossary of climbing terms"), is [Chomo Lonzo](/wiki/Chomo_Lonzo "Chomo Lonzo") (7,804 m (25,604 ft)).

fanoutqa_002141.t: Ovarian cancer :: Diagnosis :: Pathology :: Epithelial carcinoma :: chunk_0019
fanoutqa_002141.x:
Ovarian cancer :: Diagnosis :: Pathology :: Epithelial carcinoma :: chunk_0019
[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ed/Ovarian_carcinoma.JPG/330px-Ovarian_carcinoma.JPG)](/wiki/File:Ovarian_carcinoma.JPG)

A pathological specimen of ovarian carcinoma

Epithelial ovarian cancer typically presents at an advanced stage and is derived from the malignant transformation of the epithelium of the ovarian surface, peritoneum, or fallopian tube.[[68]](#cite_note-Desai14-68) It is the most common cause of gynecologic cancer death.[[68]](#cite_note-Desai14-68) There are various types of epithelial ovarian cancer, including serous tumor, endometrioid tumor, clear-cell tumor, mucinous tumor, and undifferentiated or unclassified tumors.[[69]](#cite_note-69) Annually worldwide, 230,000 women will be diagnosed and 150,000 will die.[[70]](#cite_note-Lheureux19-70) It has a 46% 5 year survival rate after diagnosis because of the advanced stage of the disease at the time of diagnosis.[[70]](#cite_note-Lheureux19-70) Typically, around 75% of patients are diagnosed as having an advanced stage of the disease because of the asymptomatic nature of its presentation.[[70]](#cite_note-Lheureux19-70) There is a genomic predisposition to epithelial ovarian cancer and the BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes have been found to be the causative genes in 65–75% of hereditary epithelial ovarian cancer.[[70]](#cite_note-Lheureux19-70)

Pierce was selected with the 10th overall pick in the [1998 NBA draft](/wiki/1998_NBA_draft "1998 NBA draft") by the [Boston Celtics](/wiki/Boston_Celtics "Boston Celtics"), a team he "despised" growing up.[[7]](#cite_note-7) He scored 19 or more points in 10 of his first 11 contests. For that year, he averaged 16.5 points and finished third in the voting for Rookie of the Year honors. In his second season, he raised his scoring average to 19.5 points per game.[[8]](#cite_note-8) In the 2000–01 season, Pierce appeared in 82 games (all starts), averaging 25.3 points, 6.4 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 1.68 steals in 38.0 minutes. He led the Celtics and finished eighth in the league in points per game and fourth in total points (2,071). He was named [NBA Player of the Month](/wiki/NBA_Player_of_the_Month "NBA Player of the Month") for March 2001 after averaging 30.3 points, 7.2 rebounds, 3.4 assists, and 1.60 steals for the month.[[6]](#cite_note-nba-bio-6)

[Mark Zuckerberg](/wiki/Mark_Zuckerberg "Mark Zuckerberg"), co-creator of Facebook, in his [Harvard](/wiki/Harvard_University "Harvard University") [dorm room](/wiki/Dorm_room "Dorm room"), November 2005

The history of Facebook traces its growth from a college networking site to a global [social networking](/wiki/Social_network "Social network") service.[[15]](#cite_note-15)

While attending [Phillips Exeter](/wiki/Phillips_Exeter "Phillips Exeter") in the early 2000s, Zuckerberg met Kris Tillery. Tillery, a one-time project collaborator with Zuckerberg, would create a school-based social networking project called Photo Address Book.[[16]](#cite_note-:0-16) Photo Address Book was a digital [face book](/wiki/Face_book "Face book"), created through a linked [database](/wiki/Database "Database") composed of student information derived from the official records of the Exeter Student Council.[[16]](#cite_note-:0-16) The database contained linkages such as name, dorm-specific landline numbers, and student [headshots](/wiki/Head_shot "Head shot").[[16]](#cite_note-:0-16)

Mark Zuckerberg built a website called "Facemash" in 2003 while attending [Harvard University](/wiki/Harvard_University "Harvard University"). The site was comparable to [Hot or Not](/wiki/Hot_or_Not "Hot or Not") and used photos from online face books, asking users to choose the 'hotter' person".[[17]](#cite_note-Harvard_Crimson_on_Facemash-17) Zuckerberg was reported and faced [expulsion](/wiki/Expulsion_(education) "Expulsion (education)"), but the charges were dropped.[[17]](#cite_note-Harvard_Crimson_on_Facemash-17)

A "face book" is a student [directory](/wiki/Directory_service "Directory service") featuring photos and personal information. Luffy first appears as a young boy in Windmill Village located in the Goa kingdom, where he befriends the pirate ["Red-Haired" Shanks](/wiki/Shanks_(One_Piece) "Shanks (One Piece)") and intends to become one himself. He accidentally eats a Devil Fruit called Gum-Gum Fruit and acquires rubber powers at the cost of being unable to swim. Shanks later saves Luffy from being devoured by a Sea King, a monstrous sea beast, at the cost of his left arm. Before departing Windmill Village, Shanks gives Luffy his treasured straw hat, on the condition that he becomes a great pirate someday and returns it to him.

Ten years later, Luffy leaves the village in a small fishing boat in search of the legendary treasure 'One Piece' to become the next King of the Pirates. Main article: [*Casino Royale* (2006 film)](/wiki/Casino_Royale_(2006_film) "Casino Royale (2006 film)")

This serves as a [reboot](/wiki/Reboot_(fiction) "Reboot (fiction)") of the series, with Bond (played by [Daniel Craig](/wiki/Daniel_Craig "Daniel Craig")) gaining his [00 status](/wiki/00_Agent "00 Agent") in the [pre-credits](/wiki/Pre-credit "Pre-credit") sequence. Bond tracks down and kills a bomb-maker and takes his mobile phone. Searching through the phone, Bond discovers a text message which he traces to Alex Dimitrios, and then on to terrorist financier [Le Chiffre](/wiki/Le_Chiffre "Le Chiffre"), who [short-sells](/wiki/Short_(finance) "Short (finance)") stock in successful companies and then engineers terrorist attacks to sink their share prices. Bond foils Le Chiffre's plan to destroy the prototype *Skyfleet* airliner, which forces Le Chiffre to set up a high-stakes poker tournament at the Casino Royale to recoup his fortune. Bond is instructed to beat Le Chiffre and is aided by a member of [HM Treasury](/wiki/HM_Treasury "HM Treasury"), [Vesper Lynd](/wiki/Vesper_Lynd "Vesper Lynd").

Bond beats Le Chiffre at the poker table, but Lynd is kidnapped by Le Chiffre after the game, as is Bond, who is captured while pursuing them; Lynd is ransomed for the money and Bond is tortured. Le Chiffre is subsequently killed by Mr. White, a liaison between Le Chiffre and a number of his clients. Bond learns that his poker winnings were never repaid to the Treasury, which Lynd was supposed to have done, and establishes that she was a double agent. Bond pursues her and is attacked by members of White's organisation: he survives, but White takes the money and Lynd sacrifices herself to save Bond, as he later finds out from M. Bond subsequently finds and captures White.

The following are amongst the oldest buildings in the world that have maintained the requirements to be such. Occupation sites with older human made structures, such as those in [Göbekli Tepe](/wiki/G%C3%B6bekli_Tepe "Göbekli Tepe") do exist, but the structures are monuments and do not meet the definition of building (which can be seen above). Many of the buildings within the list contain primarily bricks, but most importantly maintain their walls and roofs. There are numerous extant structures that survive in the [Orkney](/wiki/Orkney "Orkney") islands of Scotland, some of the best known of which are part of the [Heart of Neolithic Orkney](/wiki/Heart_of_Neolithic_Orkney "Heart of Neolithic Orkney") [World Heritage Site](/wiki/World_Heritage_Site "World Heritage Site").[[2]](#cite_note-2) The list also contains many large buildings from the Egyptian [Age of the Pyramids](/wiki/Old_Kingdom_of_Egypt "Old Kingdom of Egypt").

Main article: [*Friends* season 3](/wiki/Friends_season_3 "Friends season 3")

Season 3 takes on a significantly more serialized format. Chandler and Janice date for several episodes until Joey catches Janice kissing her soon-to-be ex-husband Gary Litman (Mark Cohen). Not wanting to destroy her family, Chandler urges Janice to go back to Gary, then becomes depressed over the breakup for several episodes. Rachel quits her job at Central Perk and begins working at Bloomingdale's, an upscale department store chain. Ross soon becomes jealous of her colleague Mark Robinson ([Steven Eckholdt](/wiki/Steven_Eckholdt "Steven Eckholdt")) and frustrated by Rachel's long work hours. She is tired of his constant jealousy and insecurity, and decides they need a relationship break.

Ross, hurt and somewhat drunk, immediately sleeps with Chloe ([Angela Featherstone](/wiki/Angela_Featherstone "Angela Featherstone")), "the hot girl from the Xerox place," causing Rachel to break up with him completely. Although Phoebe initially believes she has no family except her twin sister Ursula Buffay (Lisa Kudrow), she learns she has a half-brother, Frank Buffay Jr. ([Giovanni Ribisi](/wiki/Giovanni_Ribisi "Giovanni Ribisi")) and discovers her birth mother, Phoebe Abbott ([Teri Garr](/wiki/Teri_Garr "Teri Garr")) over the course of the season. Joey falls in love with his acting partner Kate Miller ([Dina Meyer](/wiki/Dina_Meyer "Dina Meyer")), but is jealous of her dating Marshall Townend ([Reg Rogers](/wiki/Reg_Rogers "Reg Rogers")) the director of their play. They begin a brief relationship that ends when she takes an acting job in Los Angeles.

Monica dates millionaire Pete Becker ([Jon Favreau](/wiki/Jon_Favreau "Jon Favreau")), despite her initially not being attracted to him. However, she breaks up with Pete after he is seriously hurt trying to become the [Ultimate Fighting Champion](/wiki/Ultimate_Fighting_Championship "Ultimate Fighting Championship") and refuses to quit.
